title: Minimum-service-unit mismatch inside responsibility functions
purpose: Test whether small transactions fall below the economic minimum of professional inspection/testing/fulfillment responsibility services, forcing current Jiangsu/Xuzhou actors to self-inspect, self-transport, self-coordinate or accept risk.
scan_rule: PROFESSIONAL MINIMUM PRICE != OBSERVED MICRO-UNIT GAP
MINIMUM SERVICE UNIT MISMATCH IS REAL ONLY WHEN A NAMED ACTOR CURRENTLY PERFORMS A COSTLY WORKAROUND
A solved shared-lab or micro-inspection case is a mechanism precedent, not a current opportunity
When a responsibility function can be standardized, markets often compress it toward per-batch, per-order or per-ticket pricing

patterns_tested.named_actor: 南京六城食品有限公司
observed_prior_workaround: The company maintained its own laboratory and bore equipment/personnel/consumable operating cost.
Tests outside its internal capability still had to be sent to qualified third-party institutions.
resolved_unit: A shared laboratory now provides per-variety/per-batch testing below RMB 30.
Report turnaround is about one day versus roughly three days through prior third-party testing.

patterns_tested.observed_prior_economics: Xinghua small food enterprises previously spent about RMB 140,000 per year on full testing while also lacking equipment and personnel.
patterns_tested.resolved_unit: Shared laboratories reduced annual average testing cost to about RMB 20,000 and have produced thousands of reports.

incumbent_micro_units: Current third-party inspection platforms advertise basic inspection around RMB 500-550 per visit/order and explicitly target small batches.
Service is already standardized into bounded checklists, reports and short turnaround.
SF Express sells return inspection at RMB 2-6 per ticket depending on inspection/photo combination.
Photo-return evidence is also sold per ticket.
Cross-border parcel operators advertise simple inspection around RMB 2-3 per order.
patterns_tested.meaning: Inspection/evidence responsibility can be compressed to a single logistics ticket when the task is sufficiently standardized.

incumbent_micro_units: Current providers explicitly accept a few units or a single unit into overseas-warehouse/fulfillment workflows.
Some advertise no minimum inbound quantity and no small-order surcharge.

current_route: Xuzhou publicly reports broad free training and precise quality/certification assistance for small enterprises.
Named firms in current reporting show quality problems being handled through targeted assistance rather than being stranded below a commercial service minimum.

material_learning: Minimum-service-unit mismatch inside responsibility functions is real and economically important.

However, broad repeated demand causes the market or public/shared infrastructure to compress large professional services into shared labs, per-order inspection, per-ticket evidence and single-unit fulfillment.
Price-list evidence alone is insufficient; no current named Xuzhou/Jiangsu actor remained stuck in a measurable self-service workaround after these micro-service routes were considered.

The next search must look for responsibility functions that resist micro-unit compression because each transaction still requires context, judgment or local coordination, yet the task remains bounded and low-permission.
cross_industry_result.current_best_next_truth: Fresh Scan 023 should search for bounded low-permission responsibility tasks whose fixed context-acquisition cost prevents per-ticket commoditization: small one-off local verification/acceptance where evidence must be interpreted against a transaction-specific condition. Require a named current manual workaround and reject generic field-evidence/crowdsourcing patterns already closed.
